result.title: Drift-Conditioned Structural Replay for Continual Cardiac Ultrasound Segmentation
result.summary: Conventional experience replay typically applies fixed preservation constraints to historical exemplars, overlooking variations in how learned representations, predictions, and anatomical structures change during sequential training. To address this limitation, we propose Drift-Conditioned Structural Replay Loss (DCSRL), an exemplar-adaptive supervision mechanism that regulates anatomical preservation according to source-referenced knowledge drift. DCSRL operates within a reliability-guided replay framework that selects informative historical exemplars using anatomical content and boundary characteristics while adaptively regulating replay during training. For each retained exemplar, DCSRL constructs a frozen source-task reference signature and subsequently measures changes in feature representations, class probabilities, boundary responses, and predicted anatomical structures. These complementary drift measurements are aggregated and normalized to generate bounded, exemplar-specific coefficients that dynamically adjust boundary and structural replay losses without modifying the underlying memory-selection policy. We evaluate DCSRL under sequential learning across CAMUS, CardiacNet, and EchoNet-Dynamic, comparing its performance with regularization-, distillation-, and replay-based continual-learning approaches. Experimental findings indicate that DCSRL improves overall final segmentation performance and anatomical boundary preservation, particularly under heterogeneous imaging conditions, although trade-offs remain in knowledge transfer across tasks. These findings suggest that source-referenced multidimensional drift conditioning offers a promising direction for adaptive anatomical knowledge preservation in continual cardiac ultrasound segmentation.

AI.brief_summary: 该工作面向持续学习下的心脏超声分割，提出 Drift-Conditioned Structural Replay Loss：为每个被保留样本构造冻结的源任务参考签名，度量特征、类别概率、边界响应与预测结构的变化，聚合成样本级系数以自适应调节重放监督强度。
AI.relevance_reason: 论文不涉及推理或 latent 状态生成，但其「以源任务参考签名度量多维表示漂移并据此调节监督」的做法，可能可供核查为 LVR 中视觉细节在训练中是否退化、信息坍缩程度的诊断与加权信号。
